::: {#cor-dfs-connected}
#### Testing whether a graph is connected

Let $G$ be a graph (@def-graph-vertices-edges) with no parallel edges, and let $s$ be any vertex of $G$.
Then $G$ is connected (@def-connected) if and only if `dfs(G, s)` (@def-dfs) marks every vertex of $G$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

**Only if.**
If $G$ is connected, every vertex has a walk from $s$, so every vertex is marked, by @thm-dfs-reachable.

**If.**
Suppose every vertex is marked, and let $u$ and $v$ be vertices.
By @thm-dfs-reachable, there are walks from $s$ to $u$ and from $s$ to $v$.
The edges of $G$ have no direction, so the walk from $s$ to $u$, read backward, is a walk from $u$ to $s$.
Following it with the walk from $s$ to $v$ gives a walk from $u$ to $v$.
So $G$ is connected.

:::

:::
